answer: Shared Latency Ledger. Each identity must complete a distinct sonnet-length computation whose result is checked against a per-round quartz oscillator timing signature, so answers can't be precomputed or pooled. An attacker pays serial wall-clock time and unique hardware jitter per identity; parallelism is capped by genuine clock skew, making mass registration cost real elapsed time, not money. A fable-like narrative seed varies each round to block replay.
